source_en: Home from the library. Political science reading room.
Resident returning from the university.
Bringing my notes home. Two notebooks full so far.
Checking on the emergency water rations at home.
Logged the campus changes, then the water queue. Going home.
Bringing water home to my mother and sister.
Counted the cracks in the old lecture hall. Going home.
Returning home to my mother and sister.
Taking my notebooks home. Six of them now.
Home from my engineering lab at the polytechnic.
Going home to my husband. He hates it when I am late.
Retiring from the tram depot after thirty years.
Lost my papers again. I never notice where I put things.
Taking my son to the polyclinic for his cough.
Visiting my mother's grave. She passed in the spring.
Teaching my political science seminar. Third year as lecturer.
Nothing to note. I stopped paying attention weeks ago.
Returning to the dormitory. My family lives in Kutaisi.
The paint is peeling on your booth. Just noticed.
Is the air always this thick? It feels... heavy today.
I’m just heading back. I have a lot of reading to do.
I saw a tree turn gray while I was walking. It was quite pretty.
The static on the TV... if you stare, it looks like snow.
Everything is starting to look like a photograph. Very still.
I’m going to watch the sunset. I think it’s the last one.
Do you feel the world getting thinner? I can see right through it.
The silence is beautiful. It’s the most honest thing we have.
Thanks. You should probably fix that light soon.
Try not to look at the sky for too long today.
Enjoy the view, officer. It’s quite a show.
Wait, why? I’m not sick!
A cell? That’s fine. The view is the same from anywhere.
Isolation is just a head start on the end. I don't mind.
Wait... what are you doing?!?
Wait... No, please!
Wait... mommy!
This is a mistake. I have notes. I can prove this is a mistake.
Fine. At least in here I can keep counting without interruption.
Wait, are those water stains on the ceiling? That pattern is wrong.
No... I still had variables I hadn’t... I still hadn’t found the...
The pattern... there was a pattern... I almost had it...
I was so close... so close to figuring it all out...
Where are you coming from?
The university library. Political science reading room. They closed it around me at seven. Their clock runs two minutes slow.
Campus. Almost empty. I walk the same route and log what changed since yesterday. Then the water queue.
The old lecture halls. Nobody teaches anymore. I sat in the third row and counted the cracks. Forty-one.
The medical institute. Second-year anatomy. Very demanding, but I like the precision.
The bread queue, then home. I live alone now. It is quieter for my notes.
The university. Full lecture schedule today. The campus is busy again. Everyone came back.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Tired. I keep late hours with my notes. That is stress, not a symptom. I checked.
Hair in the brush every morning. I count the strands. Thirty-two today. The polyclinic says not to worry.
I bruise when I barely touch things. And I do not sleep. The numbers keep going when I close my eyes.
Nothing. I sleep ten hours a night and never think about anything. I barely notice what goes on.
Nothing. I am twenty-three, officer. My body recovers fast.
Fine. I stopped counting things weeks ago. I burned the notebooks. I feel much better.
The paint on your booth is peeling in the top left corner. That has been wrong for weeks.
The light in here flickers on a three-second interval. Has that always been the case?
You processed the last person seventeen seconds faster than me. Just something I noticed.
I have been counting the people coming through here. The number is down thirty percent from last week.
There is something wrong with the way the shadows fall in here today. The angle is off.
The intervals are getting shorter. Something is accelerating. I have the data if you want it.
The patterns are all converging now. I thought finding the pattern would be a relief. It is not.
I have filled six notebooks. I do not know who they are for anymore.
The numbers do not stop. Even when I close my eyes. Especially then.
